recentItems.title: Capturing 9/11: Bill Biggart's Final Images
recentItems.description:
On 11th September 2001, photojournalist Bill Biggart headed to the World Trade Center to document the unfolding attacks. Bill Biggart tragically passed away when the North Tower collapsed, but he left behind a remarkable final record of the day. Featuring testimony from his widow, Wendy Doremus, and photographs recovered from the damaged camera found in the rubble, this film tells the story behind some of the last images taken at Ground Zero, now available to see at IWM London.

00:00 The Morning of 9/11
01:06 Bill goes to Lower Manhattan
01:25 The South Tower is Hit
03:08 The South Tower Collapses

recentItems.title: What was it really like in Iraq after Desert Storm?
recentItems.description:
Bestselling Author and former war correspondent, Wendy Holden, talks about her time reporting from Iraq after Desert Storm, and shares her personal collection of never before seen photographs. 

Learn more about Wendy's work and explore her books: www.wendyholden.com

00:00 - Introduction
00:21 - How did you become a war correspondent?
01:05 - When were you sent to Iraq?
01:45 - What were the dangers of the job?
02:40 - What's a common misconception about the job?
03:17 - What did you do once you arrived?
04:33 - Do you approach reporting differently from a warzone?
05:25 - Who else did you work with?
06:26 - How did you send your articles back to the paper?
06:54 - Why was there a civil war in Iraq?
08:08 - Did you take all of the photos?
08:41 - How could you tell what was true?
10:21 - Did you have any close calls?
12:02 - What's the story behind this photo?
12:48 - What things were you taken to see?
14:36 - How have these experiences affected you?
16:22 - How does it feel to see these photos again?
17:10 - How do your experiences inform your writing?
